title: MotorStorm: Apocalypse
subtitle: A race through a city coming apart
summary: MotorStorm: Apocalypse is Evolution Studios' PlayStation 3 racing game, first released in Australia on 17 March 2011. body: MotorStorm: Apocalypse is Evolution Studios' PlayStation 3 racing game, first released in Australia on 17 March 2011. The festival moves into an abandoned city damaged by a natural disaster, where the route can change while the competitors are still using it. Buildings collapse, surfaces break and streets become unstable parts of the race. Three riders provide perspectives on the event across different difficulty levels. The setting replaces Pacific Rift's island with an urban course whose destruction is planned into the timing of the competition.

A course is not always a fixed arrangement to memorise. A collapse can expose another path or remove the one a racer expected to follow, asking the player to read movement in the scenery as well as the vehicles ahead. Different classes still compete together, carrying different advantages through the city's narrow and open sections. Boost supplies a temporary burst of speed at the risk of overheating. Knowing when to commit matters particularly when the route itself is moving, falling or opening beneath the approaching field.

Apocalypse expanded local play with four-player split-screen and offered online races with sixteen competitors, alongside vehicle customisation and progression features. Its release coincided with the 2011 earthquake and tsunami in Japan, leading Sony to postpone launches in several regions. The Australian launch went ahead before further shipments were halted. That timing became a significant part of the release's history, separate from the fictional disaster built into its courses. Its music combined orchestral and electronic contributors, supporting a racing game organised around sudden changes in speed, scenery and available space.
